title: A letter to Duke Wilhelm V of Bavaria, 12 June 1583, in a Latin-letter cipher, BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.274-277 (DECODE R9424; catalogue 161)

steps.what: Web search for KAA 4591 and Augurelio ciphers
DECODE record list from the API dump (141 records in the volume); images of the 14 targets and 30 neighbouring keys fetched with the cookie
Constrained homophonic annealing with de-modern on R9424
R9422 (1582-83) Latin-letter alphabet applied to R9424
Annealing with nulls allowed on R9424 (de-1500s, homophone caps; also Latin and Italian): failed

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from kaa4591 (catalogue 161), whose fourteen records are letters in at least six systems: System A′ stays in kaa4591; Łaski's System B is kaa4591b; R9325 is fulda1576; R9367, R9416, R9424 and R9319 are r9367, r9416, r9424 and r9319; R9291 is a key fragment.

Ryan Xu (ry-xu, with Claude Opus 5.5, outside the project; issue #89) recovered the key ciphertext-only from r9424/transcription.txt: -ka = -en (k=e, a=n), -kz = -er, then short words (zka den, rwkz aber, zok die, i4a von, noc nit), confirmed by long words (zoe/onisrco4ake dissimulationes, oazo3aco4aka indignationen, wkedDrozkaDroc beschaidenhait); '/' = double the previous letter; nulls at word edges. 146 of 169 cipher words read directly, 15 more with a one-sign emendation.

Ryan Xu's control: 65% of cipher words of 4+ signs decode to a word of a 135k-type 16th-century German lexicon (DTA) under the key, against a median 8% (max 24%) for 40 shuffled keys of the same ambiguity.

Ryan Xu's from-scratch annealing (no cribs, glosses or nulls; DTA 1500-1599 4-gram model, at most 3 signs per letter): seed 2 recovers 11 signs covering 70% of sign tokens, seed 1 8 signs (52%), seed 3 stuck; an unconstrained run collapsed to e/n/r text, the trap that defeated the 21 Sept annealing.
The contemporary glosses on f.275r checked against the key: der, thumbrobst, Wirtzburg, Hildesheim agree; "den nonnen haben" is namen in the cipher; zodDcw3, glossed Aichstet, does not decode to it.

Ryan Xu's 15 one-sign emendations checked on the DECODE images (P1, P3, full resolution): 9 settled by the image (looped d read as s/o in auch, confusion, nachgeben, durch, fructus; s-form read as e in muglich; r-form read as z in allain; first sign w in befinde; cross mark, not 4, before belaitten), suspi[c]tion withdrawn (the image gives suspition), the rest kept as supplied or uncertain letters (gr[o]ss, sti[f]t, cöl[ni]sche, [?magna], [?wünschen], [?weihb.]). 'Sl' on f.275r is the clear sigil Si. Corrections in r9424/R9424_corrections.tsv.

Look-alike merges checked: in the aligned words z stands for d 37 times and r 37 times; on the image the d-form has a hooked or tailed top and the r-form is a flat-footed 2 (zizoD durch, droakz/zka, drok3ei/keka; about a dozen spot-checked, not all 92 re-labelled). n = m 22, n 4, u/v a few; r = a 45, r 2. Letters resting on the other member of a merged label: 43 of 631 aligned letters (6.8%) on the transcription labels, about 1% with the two z forms kept apart.

Reading built word by word on the images in the writer's spelling (regirt, ghen, gefurt, muglich, suspition), holes marked: r9424/R9424_reading.md, English in R9424_en.md. read_share 0.928 (v10_relabel.share: 218 words, 17 holes): coherent sentences, under the 95% bar, so read in part.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 712 tokens, 23 types, de-1500s order 4: reading -2.798 per letter; polyphonic: 15% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

docs/_validate.py on 712 sign tokens of the 126 directly read words (targets/r9424/validation.tsv, de-1500s): verdict not applicable, polyphony 0.147, because the transcription labels z, n and r each cover two glyphs; re-labelling the z forms on the images would make the test applicable.

Ryan Xu's write-up with his English translation copied into xu2026/reading.md with his permission (issue #89, 25 Oct 2026); it predates the image re-read, so our English stays the one that follows the checked reading.

Ryan Xu's pointer (issue #89, 25 Oct 2026) to Lossen, Der Kölnische Krieg II (1897; BSB bsb11808949): p. 348 n. 1 quotes Dandorf's letter to the Duke of Bavaria of 13 Aug 1583 (StA. 9/5 f. 42) and resolves the sigils Ho. (Gf. Salentin), Bi. (Kf. Ernst), Si. (Paul Stor); p. 164 names Jakob von Dandorf among Ernst's escort. Both pages checked on the BSB images. The writer of this letter is very likely Dandorf (inference from the shared sigils). No change to the key or the reading; his proposed gap readings (dz, als, magna, richtig, Co., weib) are not applied or counted until checked on the images.

outcome.method_basis: Ryan Xu (ry-xu) recovered the substitution key from this repository's transcription alone (word endings, short words, long-word confirmation; shuffled-key and annealing controls), 23 Oct 2026; the project checked it on the images and built the reading.
outcome.notes: 21 Sept 2026: attempted and closed (annealing failed). 23 Oct 2026: key recovered ciphertext-only by Ryan Xu (issue #89); checked on the images; read in part, read_share 0.928. Open: two signs before geistlichen, the name in l. 21, 'eo' in l. 22, the # sign (3x), zodDcw3.

reading_review.note: Coherent sentences in the writer's spelling; key by Ryan Xu, each word checked on the DECODE images; 17 holes in 218 words. Clean sentences 0.21 on the shape reading (no 16th-century German word list), 0.905 (19 of 21) counting explicit holes only (b17_score HOLES=1).

texts.summary: An informant at the court of Ernst of Bavaria, newly elected Archbishop of Cologne, writes to Duke Wilhelm V three weeks after the election: rivalry among Ho., Fe. and Ni., Si. ruling alone at court to the anger of Cologne and Liège, a plan to bring 'Susanna' down to Cologne or Liège that would cause great scandal, and the Würzburg cathedral provostship to be resigned to a son Philipp.

prior.where: No edition or earlier decipherment found (Ryan Xu checked this repository, Cryptiana, GitHub, Leighton 1974; Immler 1999 not online). Contemporary glosses over a few words on f.275r.

human: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied; problem posed with /goal; the user asked for a period German model. No target-specific intervention. 23 Oct 2026: the key was recovered outside the project by Ryan Xu (ry-xu) with Claude Opus 5.5 from this repository's transcription and posted as issue #89; the user asked for it to be taken in and checked on the images.
